subject.title: Slack: support assistant.threads.setSuggestedPrompts for dynamic prompt suggestions

question: Should configurable and dynamic suggested prompts be added as a Slack-native OpenClaw config/message-action surface, or should dynamic prompt suggestions live in the portable Smart Replies/plugin presentation path?
rationale: Both directions are plausible: Slack owns the native assistant.threads.setSuggestedPrompts call, but the remaining request adds config and agent-facing action surface that repository policy treats as product/API direction rather than an automatic bug fix.

options.title: Use plugin path for dynamic prompts
options.body: Keep native Slack suggested prompts limited to current default seeding unless maintainers explicitly sponsor a static config, and route dynamic Smart Replies behavior through portable plugin presentation hooks.

options.title: Add Slack-native config and action
options.body: Implement channels.slack.assistantPrompts plus a bounded set-suggested-prompts message action in the Slack plugin with schema, docs, and focused tests.

options.title: Split static from dynamic
options.body: Add only a small static Slack prompt config now and leave dynamic prompt generation to Smart Replies or a later shared action decision.

recommendation.title: Use plugin path for dynamic prompts
recommendation.body: Keep native Slack suggested prompts limited to current default seeding unless maintainers explicitly sponsor a static config, and route dynamic Smart Replies behavior through portable plugin presentation hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored and landed the Slack assistant lifecycle implementation and is the strongest history-backed owner for deciding the native Slack assistant boundary.
